CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE S.VISHWAJITH SHETTY  ORAL ORDER (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE S.VISHWAJITH SHETTY) Accused Nos.2 to 6 in C.C.No.2054/2023, pending before the Court of I Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Kalaburagi,
arising out of Crime No.2/2023 registered by Kalaburagi City Women Police Station, Kalaburagi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (for short 'D.P.Act'), are before this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings in the aforesaid criminal case as against them.

sentences.text: 2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2, who is served in the matter, has remained unrepresented before this Court.

3. The FIR in Crime No.2/2023 was registered by Kalaburagi City Women Police Station, Kalaburagi against NC: 2025:KHC-K:120 Mahantesh and the petitioners herein for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information dated 06.01.2023, received from respondent No.2, who is the wife of accused No.1.

entities.text: Kalaburagi City Women Police Station, Kalaburagi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Investigation in the matter is completed and charge sheet has been filed against six persons for the aforesaid offences and the petitioners herein are arrayed as accused Nos.2 to 6 in the charge sheet.
The Trial Court after taking cognizance of the charge sheeted offences, has issued summons to the accused vide order dated 15.04.2023.
Being aggrieved by the criminal proceedings initiated against them, petitioners are before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that dispute between the husband and wife was settled before the Family Court on 05.04.2021.
The subsequent allegation is that accused No.1 had failed to take back respondent No.2 in terms of the settlement before the Family Court.
There is an inordinate delay in approaching the police and accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for respondent No.1 has opposed the petition.
He submits that there are allegations against accused No.1 and his brother about assaulting the first informant/respondent No.2.
Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition.
6. Perusal of the material available on record would go to show that marriage of accused No.1 with respondent No.2 was solemnized on 02.05.2018.

It appears that there was some dispute between the parties immediately after marriage and in the year 2019, the first informant was allegedly Mallikarjun And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136032317/
3 thrown out of the matrimonial house.

sentences.text:
Thereafter, there was a panchayat in the month of January,
2020 and subsequently the parties had also approached the jurisdictional Family Court and before the Family Court, the dispute between the husband and wife was settled.
The settlement was reported before the Family Court on 05.04.2021 and as per the terms of the settlement, accused No.1 was supposed to take back his NC: 2025:KHC-K:120 wife.
However, since he had failed to take back his wife in terms of the compromise reported before the Family Court, it appears that the wife has approached the police.
She has made an allegation that on 18.05.2022, she had approached the police since accused No.1 had failed to take back her.
On 10.06.2022, accused No.1 and his brother had allegedly assaulted her for the reason that she had approached the police.
The police complaint is filed in the present case on 06.01.2023, which is after a delay of nearly six months from the alleged date on which accused No.1 and his brother had assaulted respondent No.2.
Insofar as the earlier dispute between the parties, which is prior to 05.04.2021, the parties have already settled the dispute and settlement was reported.
Therefore, the allegations made in the first information with regard to the incidents, which have occurred on 05.04.2021 cannot be looked into in the present case.
In the first information, no specific allegation is made as against accused Nos.2 to 6 and in spite of the same, charge sheet has been filed against all accused persons.

Perusal of the first information as well as the charge sheet would clearly go to show that allegations made against the petitioners herein, who are arrayed as accused Nos.2 to 6 are omnibus in nature and even in respect of the incident that had occurred on 10.06.2022, no specific overt-act has been alleged against anyone of the accused and there is inordinate delay in approaching the police.
8.

Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that continuation of the criminal proceedings as against the relatives of accused No.1, who is the husband of respondent No.2, amounts to abuse process of law.

Accordingly, following order is passed:
ORDER
The criminal petition is allowed.

The entire proceedings in C.C.No.2054/2023, pending before the Court of I Additional Civil Judge and JMFC,
Kalaburagi, arising out of Crime No.2/2023 NC: 2025:KHC-K:120 registered by Kalaburagi City Women Police Station, Kalaburagi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of D.P.Act, as against the petitioners/accused Nos.2 to 6 stands quashed.
